answer: In an island marketplace, agents selling services such as cipher analysis or falcon tracking must lock 100 tokens per identity for 30 days. Jobs are assigned by lottery, with each agent's chance proportional to its locked stake. Splitting 1,000 tokens among ten identities gives the same total chance as staking them under one name. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, paying the capital cost for the full lock period.
